is_anopheles.evidence: Studies field populations of Anopheles gambiae s.l. and Anopheles funestus (page 1, Abstract; page 6, Entomological results).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper does not test or report specific target-site resistance markers; it only mentions in the discussion that 'an increase in kdr allele frequency... was observed after each spray round and the importance of insecticide resistance would be further investigated' (page 9) without presenting any assay, data, or results.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No resistance genotype or allele frequencies/counts are reported in the text, tables, or figures.

african_field_population.evidence: Indoor resting mosquitoes were collected in Karuzi Province, Burundi, between 2002 and 2005 (page 2, Methods).

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary field entomological evaluation of vector control interventions (page 2).

sub_country_location.evidence: Karuzi Province, Burundi, with named communes and coordinates/points mapped (page 2-3).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections spanned across 2002 to 2005 (nine surveys over four years) (page 2, 4).

duplicate_risk.evidence: No indication of secondary reporting of external resistance datasets.

supplement.evidence: No supplementary files containing target marker genotype data are referenced.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the impact of targeted indoor residual spraying and long-lasting insecticidal nets on indoor resting densities and sporozoite infection rates of Anopheles gambiae s.l. and An. funestus in Karuzi Province, Burundi (2002-2005). No insecticide resistance marker assays or genotype data were performed or reported.
exclusion_reasons: Does not report target insecticide resistance markers.
Does not report extractable genotype data.
